newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's UES to protest Irkutskenergo ruling.
newsitem.headline: Russia's UES to protest Irkutskenergo ruling.

text.p: Unified Energy Systems (UES) plans to protest against a decision by the State Anti-Monopoly Committee to allow a rival company to export power to Mongolia, a UES official said on Thursday.
"We can protest a committee decison in the arbitration court, and we will do so," said a UES official, who declined to be named.

The anti-monopoly committee ruled on Tuesday that UES may not interfere with Irkutskenergo power exports to Mongolia. Irkutskenergo complained that UES had restricted it from exporting electricity worth $4.5 million.

RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) said it had been forced effectively to stop the exports to ensure supplies on the national grid. UES runs the national grid in Russia and generates power of its own.

Irkutskoye AO Energetiki i Elektrifikatsii (Irkutskenergo), based in Siberia, is one of only two Russian utilities fully independent from UES, which has 49-100 percent stakes in 68 of its 71 local power companies, or "energos".
"We will keep exporting power to Mongolia now. If UES plans to protest the committee decision in the court, we will be there to prove that we are right," said an Irkutskenergo official.

The two companies have been in a dispute about the ownership of three lucrative hydro-electric power stations now operated by Irkutskenergo, and UES also has its eyes on the 40 percent government stake in Irkutskenergo.
